log.why: Ticket 1 expires sooner; testing {fliC, gyrA} (posterior 0.450) maximizes information gain and separates top candidates.
Ticket 2 has no plate growing; E3 splits its cumulative posterior 0.612 vs 0.388 for maximum information gain.
Ticket 1 has less time left and E0 tests metJ (0.548 posterior), nearly halving uncertainty and confirming the lead if positive.
Testing 1 µM on Ticket 2 splits its 0.582 cumulative posterior at or below 1 µM against 0.418 above, maximizing information gain.
Start bisecting Ticket 3 at 10 uM (0.438 vs 0.562 split) so an incubator runs while we publish Ticket 1.
Ticket 2 has 0.730 posterior on 3 µM; testing E3 refines <=3 µM vs >3 µM while utilizing a free incubator.
Test 1 µM on Ticket 2 to distinguish 3 µM (0.831) from lower thresholds while starting incubation before publishing Ticket 1.
metJ has 0.932 posterior with 23s left; publishing now secures high expected points before the deadline.
Ticket 2 has a 0.961 posterior for 3 µM and only 18 s left, so publishing now locks in a high-confidence win.
Ticket 3 has only 36 s left, and testing 30 uM splits the 0.444 vs 0.556 posterior mass most evenly.
Ticket 4 has 44 s left and flat posteriors; E11 splits the hypotheses nearly in half (0.473 vs 0.527) while Ticket 3 incubates.
Ticket 3 has 11 s left with 100 µM leading at 0.540 after E4/E5; too little time to incubate another plate.
Ticket 4 has 20s left; running E0 tests fliC (0.365) to separate it from hisG (0.391) before publishing.
While Ticket 4 incubates, testing {dnaK, lacZ} on Ticket 5 cleanly splits its posterior (0.445 vs 0.555) to narrow five genes.
Testing trpE directly targets the leading hypothesis (0.351) in Ticket 5, allowing rapid resolution and publication before the round ends.
Waiting 6 s for Ticket 5 E0 result leaves 8 s to publish; a new run will not finish before round end.
Only 3 s remain in the round, and sodA leads Ticket 5 at 0.457 posterior with positive expected publishing value.
